frequency_question: How often do central banks successfully complete the procedural pipeline for a secondary reserve ratio mandate within a four-month execution window once the policy decision to initiate the pipeline is made?
membership_rule: Members are defined as documented administrative cycles where a central bank initiated, drafted, tested IT systems with commercial banks, and formally notified an incremental reserve ratio requirement within 120 days. Excluded are permanent structural changes to baseline reserve requirements that take years of legislative or phased regulatory transitions.

cases.name: People's Bank of China Reserve Requirement Ratio adjustment for targeted liquidity (typical fast cycle)
Central Bank of Sri Lanka Statutory Reserve Ratio emergency adjustment

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 3 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 3 named deep-dive cases representing fast-track liquidity tool deployment; universe of similar emerging market ad-hoc reserve ratio tweaks is estimated at approximately 15 instances.
known_gaps: Excludes minor operational delays where implementation was pushed past 120 days due to software integration failures.
skeleton: Regulatory process cycles for short-notice liquidity instruments across emerging market central banks over the past three decades.
multiplier: 3 observed rapid-deployment events / 3 completed within the operational timeline constraint
validity_reason: Central bank digital infrastructure and regulatory notification mechanisms remain relatively stable over 4-year horizons.
